mainTopic: Flawed meal-offering vows and the word "מנחה"; the sixty-עשרון limit for one כלי and why; exact measures of the חכמים; the blood of a dead mule.
overview: The amud opens with זעירי's rule: a flawed vow for a מנחה still counts only if the person said the word "מנחה". רבא challenges this from several cases in the משנה. רב נחמן answers each time that the person did say "מנחה", and רבי שמעון's exemption is explained by רבי יוסי's view that a person's last words also count. A new משנה then teaches that a person may bring up to sixty עשרונים in one כלי. Someone who vows sixty-one splits them, sixty in one כלי and one in another. The משנה bases this on the ציבור's largest daily total of sixty-one, but רבי שמעון says the real reason is that only up to sixty can be mixed with oil. The גמרא repeats this debate between רבי יהודה בר אילעאי and רבי שמעון. רבי שמעון brings a פסוק and shows that every measure of the חכמים has a sharp cutoff, and רבי זירא explains that a מנחה must at least be fit for mixing. The amud ends with a story about measuring a dead mule's blood, a challenge that the blood of a נבילה is טהור, and רבי ביבי's silence, which he explains with רבי חנין's teaching about living without security over food.

steps.title: זעירי limits the rule to someone who said the word meal offering
steps.stepSummary: זעירי rules that the משנה's leniency (the vow still counts) applies only if the person said the word "מנחה".
steps.simpleTranslation: זעירי said: The rule was taught only where he said "meal offering." But if he did not say "meal offering," the vow does not take effect.
steps.whatsHappening: זעירי adds a limit to the משנה's ruling that a flawed vow for a מנחה still counts. It only counts if the person actually used the word "מנחה".
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה said a vow like "a מנחה from barley" still obligates him to bring a proper wheat מנחה. זעירי says this works only because he said "מנחה", which is a real offering. If he only named the flawed ingredient and never said "מנחה", there is nothing valid to obligate him.

keyTerms.meaning: They only taught this in the case of... (a formula that limits a ruling)
Meal offering, a flour offering brought in the בית המקדש

steps.whyThisMatters: This rule is what the rest of the passage tests.

phrases.english: Ze'eiri said:
They taught this only where he said "meal offering,"
phrases.notes: "This" is the משנה's ruling that a flawed meal-offering vow still counts.

phrases.english: but if he did not say "meal offering" — no.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Comments on the משנה's ruling about flawed meal-offering vows.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A flawed meal-offering vow takes effect only if the word "מנחה" was said.

steps.title: Challenge from the case of plain flour
steps.stepSummary: רבא challenges רב נחמן from the משנה's case of someone who vowed plain flour and must bring fine flour.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן was sitting and teaching this rule. רבא challenged him: "Flour": he must bring fine flour. Isn't that a case where he did not say "meal offering"?
steps.whatsHappening: While רב נחמן teaches זעירי's rule, רבא challenges it from a case in the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה says someone who vowed "flour" must bring fine flour, so his vow counts. רבא assumes he only said "flour" and never said "מנחה". If so, the vow counts without the word "מנחה", which goes against זעירי.

keyTerms.meaning: A teaching or ruling
Plain, coarse flour, which is not fit for a מנחה
Fine flour, the kind a מנחה requires
Is it not...? (used to suggest how to read a source)

phrases.english: Rav Nachman was sitting
and teaching this ruling.
phrases.notes: "This ruling" is זעירי's rule from step 1.

phrases.english: Rava raised an objection to Rav Nachman:
"Flour": he must bring fine flour,
is it not where he did not say "meal offering"?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks זעירי's rule from step 1.
steps.kashyaTarget: זעירי's requirement that the word "מנחה" be said
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה's plain-flour case seems to have no mention of "מנחה", yet the vow counts.

steps.title: Answer: he did say meal offering
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן answers that the flour case is one where he said "a מנחה of flour".
steps.simpleTranslation: No. It is a case where he said "meal offering."
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן answers that the משנה's case involves someone who did say "מנחה".
steps.deeperAnalysis: Read the case as "I take on a מנחה of plain flour." He used the word "מנחה", so the case fits זעירי's rule.

phrases.english: No, it is where he said "meal offering."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 2.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterprets the case in the משנה
steps.terutzMaskana: He said "a מנחה of flour", so זעירי stands.

steps.title: Challenge from the case without oil and frankincense
steps.stepSummary: רבא challenges again from the משנה's case of a vow without oil and frankincense.
steps.simpleTranslation: "Without oil and frankincense": he must bring oil and frankincense. Isn't that a case where he did not say "meal offering"?
steps.whatsHappening: רבא brings a second case from the משנה with the same challenge.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The vow still counts, and he must add oil and frankincense. רבא suggests he never said "מנחה", which would again go against זעירי.

keyTerms.meaning: Oil
Frankincense, normally placed on a מנחה
What, is it not...?

phrases.english: "Without oil and frankincense":
he must bring oil and frankincense.
What, is it not where he did not say "meal offering"?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second challenge to זעירי, built the same way as step 2.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The vow seems to count without the word "מנחה".

steps.title: Same answer for the oil and frankincense case
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן again says the case is one where he said "מנחה".
steps.simpleTranslation: No. It is a case where he said "meal offering."
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן gives the same answer: he said "a מנחה without oil and frankincense".
steps.deeperAnalysis: Because the word "מנחה" was said, this case also fits זעירי's rule.

phrases.english: No, it is where he said "meal offering."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 4.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterprets the case in the משנה
steps.terutzHavaAmina: He said only "without oil and frankincense".
steps.terutzMaskana: He said "a מנחה without oil and frankincense".

steps.title: Challenge from the case of half a tenth
steps.stepSummary: רבא challenges a third time from the משנה's case of a vow of half an עשרון.
steps.simpleTranslation: "Half a tenth": he must bring a full tenth. Isn't that a case where he did not say "meal offering"?
steps.whatsHappening: רבא brings a third case from the משנה, with the same challenge.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A vow of half an עשרון still obligates a full עשרון. רבא suggests he never said "מנחה", which would contradict זעירי.

keyTerms.meaning: A tenth of an איפה, the smallest amount for a מנחה
Half
Whole, complete

phrases.english: "Half a tenth":
he must bring a complete tenth,
what, is it not where he did not say "meal offering"?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A third challenge to זעירי, built the same way as steps 2 and 4.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The vow seems to count without the word "מנחה".

steps.title: Same answer for the half tenth case
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן again answers that he said "מנחה".
steps.simpleTranslation: No. It is a case where he said "meal offering."
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן answers the third challenge the same way as the first two.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He said "a מנחה of half an עשרון", so זעירי's rule still holds for all three cases in the משנה.
steps.whatToRemember: זעירי: a flawed meal-offering vow counts only if the word "מנחה" was said. רבא challenged three times (plain flour, no oil and frankincense, half an עשרון). Each time רב נחמן answered that the person did say "מנחה".

phrases.english: No, it is where he said "meal offering."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 6.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterprets the case in the משנה
steps.terutzMaskana: He said "a מנחה of half a tenth", so זעירי's rule stands.

steps.title: Challenge from the case of a tenth and a half
steps.stepSummary: רבא argues that רב נחמן's answer does not fit the סיפא. If the vow included 'מנחה', the extra 'half a tenth' means nothing, so why bring two?
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, look at the last case: 'a tenth and a half – he brings two.' Once he said 'מנחה' he owes one tenth. When he says 'half a tenth', that means nothing!
steps.whatsHappening: רבא challenges רב נחמן a fourth time, now from the last case of the משנה: someone who vowed a tenth and a half.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב נחמן has been saying that every case involved the word 'מנחה'. In that case the person owes one full עשרון, and the words 'half a tenth' are meaningless. So the משנה's ruling that he brings two עשרונים makes no sense.

keyTerms.meaning: If so: the opening of a challenge built on the last answer
The last clause of the משנה
A tenth of an איפה of flour, the smallest amount for a מנחה
He said nothing: the words have no legal effect

phrases.english: If so, say the last clause:
A tenth and a half – he should bring two.
Once he said 'meal offering,'
he became obligated in a tenth;
when he says 'half a tenth,'
he is saying nothing.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Fourth challenge in the series, now aimed at the סיפא.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב נחמן's claim that every case of the משנה involved the word 'מנחה'.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If 'מנחה' already obligates one עשרון, then 'half a tenth' adds nothing. The ruling of two עשרונים cannot be explained.

steps.title: The case is half a tenth followed by a tenth
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן explains that the person said 'a מנחה of half a tenth and a tenth'. 'מנחה' gives one tenth, and the separate later 'tenth' gives another.
steps.simpleTranslation: No, the case is where he said 'I must bring a מנחה of half a tenth and a tenth.' Saying 'מנחה' made him owe one tenth. 'Half a tenth' meant nothing. When he then said 'a tenth', he brings another tenth.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן answers by showing the exact order of words in the vow that would make two עשרונים necessary.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The order of the words is key. 'מנחה' already creates one full עשרון, and 'half a tenth' is ignored. The final word 'tenth' is a new, separate obligation, so the total is two.

keyTerms.meaning: It is only needed for: introduces the specific case where the ruling applies
It is upon me: the standard wording of a vow
He then said again: words added afterward
Another, an additional one

phrases.english: No, it is needed where he said:
'It is upon me to bring a meal offering of half a tenth and a tenth,'
for since he said 'meal offering,'
he became obligated in a tenth;
when he said 'half a tenth,'
he said nothing;
when he then said 'a tenth,'
he brings another tenth.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 8.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Narrowing the case to a specific order of words
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The vow was 'a tenth and a half', so the half should be meaningless.
steps.terutzMaskana: The vow was 'מנחה, half a tenth, and a tenth'. The final 'tenth' is a second obligation, so he brings two.

steps.title: Why does רבי שמעון exempt him?
steps.stepSummary: If every case included the word 'מנחה', why does רבי שמעון rule that the person owes nothing at all?
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, רבי שמעון exempts him because he did not vow the way people normally vow. Why? He said 'מנחה'!
steps.whatsHappening: רבא raises a new challenge from רבי שמעון's opinion in the same משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב נחמן's reading has the person saying 'מנחה', a perfectly valid vow. So why would רבי שמעון cancel the whole vow just because extra, improper words were added later?

keyTerms.meaning: Exempts, frees from obligation
In the normal way people make donations
Why?

phrases.english: If so, Rabbi Shimon exempts him,
because he did not pledge in the manner of those who pledge –
why?
phrases.notes: Since he said 'מנחה', the vow should still count.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the case wording is settled, the challenge moves to רבי שמעון's ruling.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי שמעון's exemption in the משנה, read according to רב נחמן.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Saying 'מנחה' should create a valid obligation, so a full exemption seems impossible.

steps.title: רבי שמעון follows רבי יוסי: final words count too
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון holds like רבי יוסי, who says a person is also bound by the end of his words. So the improper ending cancels the vow.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: רבי שמעון said this following the view of רבי יוסי, who says: a person's final words also take hold.
steps.whatsHappening: The challenge is answered by linking רבי שמעון to רבי יוסי's general principle.
steps.deeperAnalysis: We usually judge a statement by its first words. רבי יוסי says the last words matter too. Since this vow ended with words that do not fit a proper מנחה, the vow as a whole is not valid, so רבי שמעון exempts him.

keyTerms.meaning: According to the approach of
The end of his words
Takes hold, binds: the words take legal effect

steps.whatToRemember: רב נחמן's reading survives every challenge. In each case the person said 'מנחה', and רבי שמעון's exemption is explained by רבי יוסי's rule that a person's last words also count.

phrases.english: Rava said:

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בְּשִׁיטַת רַבִּי יוֹסֵי אֲמָרָהּ,
phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon stated it according to the approach of Rabbi Yosei,
who said:
A person is bound also by the conclusion of his words.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בְּשִׁיטַת רַבִּי יוֹסֵי אֲמָרָהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge about רבי שמעון.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Linking a תנא to a known general view
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Saying 'מנחה' first should lock in a valid vow.
steps.terutzMaskana: According to רבי יוסי the ending also counts, so the improper ending cancels the vow.

steps.title: New משנה: up to sixty tenths in one vessel
steps.stepSummary: A person may vow a מנחה of sixty עשרונים and bring it all in one vessel.
steps.simpleTranslation: A person may donate a מנחה of sixty tenths and bring it in one vessel. (If he said 'I must bring sixty tenths', he brings them in one vessel.)
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It teaches the largest single מנחה a person may bring in one vessel.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Sixty עשרונים can all be mixed and offered together as one מנחה. The words in brackets repeat the same idea for someone who said 'sixty tenths' without the word 'מנחה'.

keyTerms.meaning: Short for מתניתין, 'our משנה'
Donates, pledges voluntarily
One vessel: all offered together as a single מנחה

phrases.english: MISHNA:

phrases.aramaic: מִתְנַדֵּב אָדָם מִנְחָה שֶׁל שִׁשִּׁים עִשָּׂרוֹן,
phrases.english: A person may pledge a meal offering of sixty tenths,
and bring it in one vessel.
(If he said: 'It is upon me to bring sixty tenths,'
phrases.notes: Some versions leave out the words in round brackets. They just repeat the same rule.

phrases.english: he brings it in one vessel.)

steps.triggerLanguage: מִתְנַדֵּב אָדָם מִנְחָה שֶׁל שִׁשִּׁים עִשָּׂרוֹן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה on a new topic.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A single מנחה of up to sixty עשרונים may be brought in one vessel.

steps.title: Sixty-one tenths must be split, like the ציבור's largest day
steps.stepSummary: Someone who vows sixty-one brings sixty in one vessel and one in another. The reason is that sixty-one is the most the ציבור brings in one day.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he said 'I must bring sixty-one', he brings sixty in one vessel and one in another vessel. That is because the ציבור brings sixty-one on the first day of סוכות when it falls on שבת.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives the limit. Above sixty, the vow is split into two vessels, and the משנה gives a reason from the ציבור's offerings.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ציבור's highest total in one day is sixty-one עשרונים. That happens on the first day of סוכות falling on שבת, when the offerings of the חג, of שבת and the daily offerings combine. The משנה treats that total as the ceiling. The next step explains that a private person stays one below it, so sixty is his limit for one כלי and the sixty-first goes in a separate כלי.

keyTerms.meaning: The community, whose offerings are brought for all of Israel
The first day of the Festival (סוכות)
For so it is: introduces the reason

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think sixty-one is forbidden altogether. He still brings all sixty-one, just not in one vessel: sixty in one and one in another.
steps.whatToRemember: Sixty עשרונים is the most for one vessel. Any vow above sixty is split, based on the ציבור's largest daily total of sixty-one.

phrases.english: If he said: 'It is upon me to bring sixty-one,'
he brings sixty in one vessel,
and one in another vessel,
phrases.notes: Literally 'in one vessel', but it means a second, separate vessel.

phrases.english: for so the community brings,
on the first festival day of Sukkot
that falls on Shabbat,
sixty-one.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִם אָמַר הֲרֵי עָלַי שִׁשִּׁים וְאֶחָד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the משנה by setting the limit and giving its reason.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A vow of sixty-one עשרונים is split into sixty and one, since the ציבור's largest daily total is sixty-one.

steps.title: An individual brings one less than the community
steps.stepSummary: The משנה finishes its reason: it is enough for a יחיד to bring one עשרון less than the ציבור.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is enough for an individual to be one less than the community.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה finishes the reason it began giving in the last step. The most the ציבור brings in one day is sixty-one עשרונים, so a יחיד stops at sixty.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 13 said that sixty-one is the most the ציבור ever brings in one day. This line completes the thought: a private person should not match the ציבור, so his limit is one below theirs. That is why sixty is the most that can go into one כלי.

keyTerms.meaning: It is enough for him
An individual, one private person
The community as a whole, whose קרבנות are brought for everyone

phrases.english: It is enough for the individual
that he is less than the community by one.
phrases.notes: "One" means one עשרון: sixty for the individual, compared with sixty-one for the ציבור.

steps.triggerLanguage: דַּיּוֹ לַיָּחִיד שֶׁהוּא פָּחוֹת מִן הַצִּיבּוּר אֶחָד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the reason that step 13 began for the sixty-עשרון limit.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A יחיד's limit for one כלי is one עשרון below the ציבור's daily maximum of sixty-one, so it is sixty.

steps.title: רבי שמעון rejects the comparison to the community
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון points out that the ציבור's sixty-one עשרונים are never mixed together, so they cannot serve as the model.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמעון said: But some of these are for the bulls and some are for the lambs, and they are not mixed with each other!
steps.whatsHappening: רבי שמעון attacks the reason the משנה just gave. He says the ציבור's sixty-one עשרונים are not one big batch at all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The reason depended on the ציבור bringing sixty-one together. רבי שמעון notes that those עשרונים belong to different animals, bulls and lambs, and are kept separate. So there is no 'sixty-one in one batch' to compare the יחיד to.

keyTerms.meaning: Bulls (here, the bulls of the מוספין)
Lambs
Mixed together (flour mixed with oil)

phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon said:
But are not these for the bulls,
and those for the lambs,
and they are not mixed with each other!
phrases.notes: Each animal's מנחה is mixed on its own, so the ציבור never has sixty-one עשרונים in one mixture.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the reason given in steps 13-14.
steps.kashyaTarget: The reason that the יחיד's limit comes from the ציבור's sixty-one עשרונים.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ציבור's sixty-one are split among different animals and never mixed as one batch, so the comparison does not hold.

steps.title: רבי שמעון's own reason: sixty is the most that can be mixed
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון explains that the limit is sixty because up to sixty עשרונים can be mixed properly.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, up to sixty can be mixed.
steps.whatsHappening: After rejecting the משנה's reason, רבי שמעון gives his own reason for the sixty limit.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי שמעון agrees that the limit is sixty, but for a practical reason: mixing. Up to sixty עשרונים can still be mixed properly with the oil. Beyond that, proper mixing can no longer be done.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather (brings in a new explanation in place of the rejected one)
To be mixed properly with the oil

steps.whyThisMatters: Both sides agree that the limit is sixty. They only argue about why, and that is what sets up the next challenge.

phrases.english: Rather, up to sixty
can be mixed.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a new reason in place of the one רבי שמעון just rejected.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The sixty-עשרון limit exists because only up to sixty עשרונים can be mixed properly.

steps.title: The חכמים ask whether one extra עשרון can really matter
steps.stepSummary: The חכמים ask in surprise: can sixty be mixed but sixty-one cannot?
steps.simpleTranslation: They said to him: Sixty can be mixed, and sixty-one cannot be mixed?!
steps.whatsHappening: The חכמים challenge רבי שמעון's reason. They find it hard to believe that a single extra עשרון makes mixing impossible.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the limit is about how much can physically be mixed, it seems strange to draw such a sharp line. Sixty and sixty-one are almost the same amount, so why would one work and the other fail?

keyTerms.meaning: Sixty-one
They cannot be mixed

phrases.english: They said to him:
Sixty can be mixed,
and sixty-one cannot be mixed?!

steps.triggerLanguage: שִׁשִּׁים נִבְלָלִין, וְשִׁשִּׁים וְאֶחָד אֵין נִבְלָלִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the reason רבי שמעון gave in step 16.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי שמעון's claim that mixing works up to exactly sixty.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A one-עשרון difference seems too small to decide whether mixing is possible, so an exact cutoff looks arbitrary.

steps.title: All measures of the חכמים have exact cutoffs, like a מקוה
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון answers that every measure set by the חכמים has a sharp line, like the forty סאה of a מקוה.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to them: All the measures of the חכמים are like this. In forty סאה a person can immerse, but in forty סאה minus a tiny קורטוב he cannot immerse.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי שמעון defends his reason with a well-known example. A מקוה works with forty סאה but fails if even a tiny bit is missing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A measure has to stop somewhere, and wherever it stops, one tiny amount will make the difference. That is normal for every fixed amount in הלכה. So a sharp line between sixty and sixty-one is not a problem.

keyTerms.meaning: The fixed measures set by the חכמים
Forty סאה, the minimum amount of water for a מקוה
A very tiny measure
Immerses to become טהור

steps.whatToRemember: Both תנא קמא and רבי שמעון agree the limit is sixty in one כלי. They differ on the reason, and רבי שמעון teaches that any fixed measure has an exact cutoff, just like a מקוה.

phrases.english: He said to them:
All the measures of the Sages are so –
in forty se'a one immerses,
phrases.notes: He is talking about a מקוה.

phrases.english: and in forty se'a lacking a kortov
he cannot immerse in them.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 17.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A one-עשרון difference is too small to matter, so the cutoff seems arbitrary.
steps.terutzMaskana: Every fixed measure of the חכמים has an exact cutoff, as with the forty סאה of a מקוה, so sixty versus sixty-one is perfectly reasonable.

steps.title: The גמרא asks for the source of sixty in one כלי and one in another
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא opens with a question asked before רבי יהודה בר אילעאי: what is the source that someone who vows sixty-one brings sixty in one כלי and one in another?
steps.simpleTranslation: A question was asked before רבי יהודה בר אילעאי: From where do we know that one who says 'I take upon myself sixty-one' brings sixty in one vessel and one in another vessel?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins and asks for a source for the משנה's rule. This sets up the answer that will come next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה gave reasons for the limit, but the גמרא wants to know where the rule itself comes from. The question is about the exact case of a person who vows sixty-one.

keyTerms.meaning: The discussion that explains the משנה
From where? (asking for a source)
I take upon myself (the wording of a נדר)
A vessel (the כלי the מנחה is brought in)

phrases.english: GEMARA: They asked a question above,
phrases.notes: "Above" here means in front of him, the way one stands before a senior רב.

phrases.english: before Rabbi Yehuda bar Ilai:
From where do we know that one who says
"It is upon me sixty-one"
brings sixty in one vessel,
and one in another vessel?

steps.triggerLanguage: שְׁאִיל שְׁאֵילָה לְמַעְלָה מֵרַבִּי יְהוּדָה בַּר אִילְעַאי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins the גמרא's discussion of the משנה's rule from step 13.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The source for the rule that a person who vows sixty-one brings sixty in one כלי and one in another.

steps.title: The limit comes from the community's largest offering
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה בר אילעאי says the ציבור brings sixty-one עשרונים on the first day of סוכות that falls on שבת, so an individual is limited to one less: sixty.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה בר אילעאי, who always spoke first, opened and said: We find that the ציבור brings sixty-one עשרונים on the first day of סוכות when it falls on שבת. So it is enough for an individual to bring one less than the ציבור.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יהודה בר אילעאי gives the first answer to the question from step 19: the source for the limit of sixty is the most the ציבור ever brings.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The busiest day for communal מנחות is the first day of סוכות on שבת, when the total is sixty-one עשרונים. רבי יהודה reasons that an individual should not match the ציבור, so his limit is one less. That is why sixty go in one כלי and the sixty-first goes in another.

keyTerms.meaning: The first of the speakers, the one who always opened the discussion
The community, whose offerings are brought on behalf of all of Israel
An individual bringing his own offering
It is enough for him; here, he should not go beyond a certain level

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda bar Ilai opened
the first of the speakers in every place, and said:
For so we find that the community brings
on the first festival day of the Festival
that happens to fall on Shabbos
sixty-one
it is enough for the individual
that he be less than the community by one.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question raised in step 19.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The ציבור's maximum is sixty-one, so the individual's maximum is one less: sixty.

steps.title: The community's sixty-one are never mixed together
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון objects that the ציבור's sixty-one come with different animals, have different oil ratios, and are mixed at different times, so they are never mixed as one.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמעון said to him: Aren't some of these brought with bulls and rams and some with lambs? Some have a thick mixture and some a thin mixture. Some are mixed in the morning and some in the afternoon. They are not mixed together.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי שמעון attacks רבי יהודה's proof: the ציבור's sixty-one עשרונים are not one batch, so they cannot be the model for one כלי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question is about how much can go into one כלי. The ציבור's sixty-one are split three ways: by animal type, by thick or thin oil mixture, and by morning or afternoon. Since they are never mixed together, they prove nothing about the limit for one mixture.

keyTerms.meaning: Mixing the flour with the oil
Thick, with less oil compared to the flour
Thin or soft, with more oil compared to the flour
In the morning
In the afternoon, toward evening

phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon said to him:
But aren't these brought with bulls and rams,
and those with lambs?
These have a thick mixture,
and those have a thin mixture.
These are mixed in the morning,
and those are mixed in the afternoon,
and they are not mixed one with the other.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לוֹ רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן: וַהֲלֹא אֵלּוּ פָּרִים וְאֵילִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the proof given in step 20.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יהודה's comparison to the ציבור's sixty-one עשרונים
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ציבור's sixty-one are split into separate mixtures, so they cannot set the limit for one כלי.

steps.title: The חכמים ask for רבי שמעון's own reason
steps.stepSummary: The חכמים ask רבי שמעון to give his own reason for the limit.
steps.simpleTranslation: They said to him: You tell us.
steps.whatsHappening: After rejecting רבי יהודה's reason, רבי שמעון is asked for his own. This short line sets up his answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the ציבור is not the source, the limit of sixty still needs an explanation. The חכמים put the burden on רבי שמעון.

keyTerms.meaning: You say; give your own explanation

phrases.english: They said to him: "You say."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Follows the rejection in step 21 by asking for a new reason.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What is רבי שמעון's own source for the limit of sixty?

steps.title: A מנחה must be able to be mixed
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון cites 'וכל מנחה בלולה בשמן': the תורה requires a מנחה that can be mixed properly.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to them: It says, 'And every מנחה mixed with oil, or dry.' The תורה has already said: bring a מנחה that is able to be mixed.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי שמעון gives his source: a פסוק showing that a מנחה must be one that can actually be mixed with its oil.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word בלולה tells us mixing is required, so the מנחה must be an amount that can really be mixed. Combined with step 16, sixty is the most that can be mixed properly in one כלי.

keyTerms.meaning: Mixed with oil
Dry, a מנחה with no oil
Able to be mixed

steps.whyThisMatters: This becomes the real reason for the הלכה that sixty go in one כלי and the rest in another.

phrases.english: He said to them: It says
"And every meal offering mixed with oil, or dry,"
the Torah has already said:
Bring a meal offering that is able to be mixed.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the request in step 22.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The פסוק requires a מנחה that can be mixed, and sixty is the most that can be mixed.

steps.title: Can sixty really be mixed but not sixty-one?
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון is challenged: is one more עשרון really the difference between mixable and not mixable?
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: With sixty they can be mixed, but with sixty-one they cannot?!
steps.whatsHappening: רבי שמעון is asked in surprise how one extra עשרון could make the mixture impossible.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Mixing seems like a gradual thing. It sounds strange that sixty works while sixty-one completely fails. The challenge questions whether a physical limit can be that exact.

keyTerms.meaning: They are mixed (flour with oil)

phrases.english: He said to him: With sixty they are mixed,
but with sixty-one they are not mixed?!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבי שמעון's reason from step 23.
steps.kashyaTarget: The exact line between sixty and sixty-one
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: One extra עשרון should not suddenly make mixing impossible.

steps.title: Every measure of the חכמים has a sharp line
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון answers that all measures of the חכמים work this way: forty סאה of a מקוה purifies, and forty minus a tiny amount does not.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: All the measures of the חכמים are like this. In forty סאה one can immerse, but in forty סאה minus a קורטוב one cannot immerse.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי שמעון defends the exact limit by comparing it to the forty סאה of a מקוה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Measures in הלכה must stop somewhere, so a tiny difference can matter completely. A מקוה with forty סאה works, but one missing even a tiny קורטוב does not. The same applies to sixty versus sixty-one.

keyTerms.meaning: A measure set by the חכמים
A measure of volume; a מקוה needs forty of them
A very tiny measure
Immerses in a מקוה to become טהור

steps.whatToRemember: An individual may bring up to sixty עשרונים in one כלי because a מנחה must be mixable. רבי שמעון rejects the comparison to the ציבור, and he explains the exact cutoff with the rule that every measure of the חכמים has a sharp line, like forty סאה for a מקוה.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not think רבי שמעון is saying the sixty-first עשרון physically ruins the mixture. He is saying that a measure in הלכה has a fixed cutoff, even if the real-world difference is tiny.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר לוֹ: כׇּל מִדַּת חֲכָמִים כֵּן הוּא –
phrases.english: He said to him: All the measures of the Sages are like this:
in forty se'ah he immerses,
in forty se'ah lacking a kortov
he cannot immerse.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לוֹ: כׇּל מִדַּת חֲכָמִים כֵּן הוּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 24.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Comparison to a known principle about halachic measures
steps.terutzHavaAmina: One extra עשרון should not change whether the מנחה can be mixed.
steps.terutzMaskana: Halachic measures have exact cutoffs, so sixty can be mixed in one כלי and sixty-one cannot, just like forty סאה for a מקוה.

steps.title: More examples of exact cutoffs: food and cloth
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון continues his answer with two more measures that have a sharp cutoff: כביצה for טומאת אוכלין and three by three טפחים for מדרס.
steps.simpleTranslation: Food the size of an egg passes on food-impurity, but an egg minus a sesame seed does not. Cloth three by three can become impure through מדרס, but three by three minus one thread cannot.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי שמעון is still answering the challenge from step 24. He adds two more examples to show that a tiny difference can change the הלכה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Like the מקוה of forty סאה in step 25, these measures have an exact line. Even a sesame seed or a single thread below the line changes the outcome completely. So one extra עשרון can also be the line between a מנחה that can be mixed and one that cannot.

keyTerms.meaning: The size of an egg, the minimum amount of food that passes on food-impurity
Impurity of foods
A sesame seed, a tiny amount
Impurity caused when a זב sits or lies on an item
A single thread

steps.whatToRemember: The measures of the חכמים are exact. Even a tiny bit less than the measure changes the הלכה.

phrases.english: An egg-bulk of food passes on food-impurity,
an egg-bulk less a sesame seed —
does not pass on food-impurity.
A cloth three by three can become impure through מדרס,
phrases.notes: He means three טפחים by three טפחים.

phrases.aramaic: שְׁלֹשָׁה עַל שְׁלֹשָׁה חָסֵר נִימָא אַחַת –
phrases.english: three by three less one thread —
cannot become impure through מדרס.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the list of examples begun in step 25.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Analogy to other exact measures of the חכמים
steps.terutzHavaAmina: It seemed unreasonable that one עשרון could decide whether a מנחה can be mixed.
steps.terutzMaskana: All measures of the חכמים have a sharp cutoff, so one עשרון can indeed be the line.

steps.title: Why should being unable to mix matter?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why it matters if sixty-one עשרונים cannot be mixed, since a משנה teaches that a מנחה is כשר even if it was not mixed.
steps.simpleTranslation: Even if they cannot be mixed, so what? Didn't we learn that if he did not mix it, it is valid?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבי שמעון's whole reason. If mixing is not required, being unable to mix should not matter.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי שמעון said the limit exists because the מנחה must be mixable (step 23). But a משנה rules that a מנחה left unmixed is still כשר. So mixing seems to be only the ideal way, and should not set a limit.

keyTerms.meaning: Are mixed, here meaning the flour and oil can be mixed together
So what? What difference does it make?
Valid

phrases.english: And if they cannot be mixed, what of it?

phrases.aramaic: וְהָא תְּנַן: אִם לֹא בָּלַל – כָּשֵׁר!
phrases.english: But didn't we learn: if he did not mix it, it is valid!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכִי אֵין נִבְלָלִין, מַאי הָוֵי? וְהָא תְּנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the reason רבי שמעון gave in step 23.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי שמעון's reason that a מנחה must be mixable
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A משנה says an unmixed מנחה is כשר, so mixing cannot be a requirement that sets a limit.

steps.title: רבי זירא: it must at least be fit for mixing
steps.stepSummary: רבי זירא explains that skipping the mixing is allowed only when the מנחה could be mixed. If it cannot be mixed at all, it is פסול.
steps.simpleTranslation: Whatever is fit to be mixed, mixing does not hold it back. Whatever is not fit to be mixed, mixing does hold it back.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי זירא answers the challenge by separating actually mixing from being able to mix.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה that says an unmixed מנחה is כשר speaks only of a מנחה that could have been mixed. A מנחה too large to ever be mixed, like sixty-one עשרונים, is פסול. So רבי שמעון's limit still makes sense.

keyTerms.meaning: Fit to be mixed
Holds back, meaning it makes the offering invalid if missing

steps.whatToRemember: What matters is that the מנחה can be mixed. If it can, skipping the mixing does not make it פסול.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not think רבי זירא is saying mixing is required. A mixable מנחה is כשר even without mixing. Only one that cannot be mixed is פסול.
steps.whyThisMatters: This rule, that being fit for something matters even when doing it is not required, explains how רבי שמעון's limit fits with the משנה.

phrases.english: Rabbi Zeira said:
Anything that is fit for mixing —
the lack of mixing does not invalidate it,
and anything that is not fit for mixing —
the lack of mixing invalidates it.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי זֵירָא: כׇּל הָרָאוּי לְבִילָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 27.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinction between actually mixing and being able to mix
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since an unmixed מנחה is כשר, mixing seemed to have no real role.
steps.terutzMaskana: Actual mixing is not required, but the מנחה must be able to be mixed.

steps.title: The blood of רבי's mule was measured
steps.stepSummary: רבי ביבי reports in the name of רבי יהושע בן לוי that a mule of רבי's household died, and the חכמים measured its blood as a רביעית.
steps.simpleTranslation: There was a story with a mule of רבי's house that died, and the חכמים estimated its blood as a quarter-לוג.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new topic about measures: a story where the חכמים measured how much blood came out of a dead mule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The חכמים checked whether the blood reached a רביעית, which suggests the blood of a dead animal matters for טומאה. The next step will challenge exactly this point.

keyTerms.meaning: A mule
They estimated or measured
A quarter of a לוג, a standard measure for liquids

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי בִּיבִי, אָמַר רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן לֵוִי:
phrases.english: Rabbi Beivai said that Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi said:
There was an incident with a certain mule
of the house of רבי that died,
phrases.notes: רבי here is רבי יהודה הנשיא.

phrases.english: and the Sages estimated its blood as a quarter-לוג.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי בִּיבִי, אָמַר רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן לֵוִי: מַעֲשֶׂה בְּפִרְדָּה אַחַת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the measures of the מנחה to another case where the חכמים used a measure.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The חכמים measured the blood of a dead mule as a רביעית.

steps.title: But the blood of a dead animal is pure
steps.stepSummary: רבי יצחק בר ביסנא objects with a testimony that the blood of a נבילה is טהור, and a story of pilgrims wading in the blood of killed donkeys without being told they became impure.
steps.simpleTranslation: Two sages testified that the blood of a dead animal is pure. רבי יהושע בן בתירא told of wild donkeys killed for the king's lions, where pilgrims stood up to their knees in blood and no one told them anything.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the mule story. If blood of a dead animal is טהור, why would the חכמים bother measuring it?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Measuring the mule's blood suggests it could make things impure. But רבי יהושע and רבי יהושע בן בתירא testified that the blood of a נבילה is טהור. The donkey story backs this up: pilgrims about to enter the מקדש stood in the blood, and no one warned them.

keyTerms.meaning: Testified to a received tradition
The blood of animals that died without proper שחיטה
Pilgrims going up to ירושלים for the festival
A stadium or arena

steps.confusionAlert: The animal itself, the נבילה, is impure. The testimony is only about its blood.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yitzchak bar Bisna raised an objection:

phrases.aramaic: הֵעִיד רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ וְרַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן בְּתֵירָא
phrases.english: Rabbi Yehoshua and Rabbi Yehoshua ben Beteira testified
about the blood of carcasses, that it is pure,
and Rabbi Yehoshua ben Beteira said:
There was an incident where they were killing wild donkeys
phrases.notes: נוחרין means killing by stabbing, not by proper שחיטה, so the donkeys were נבילות.

phrases.english: for the lions in the king's arena,
and the festival pilgrims were sinking
up to their knees in the blood,
and they did not say anything to them.
phrases.notes: The חכמים never warned the pilgrims that they had become impure.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the mule story of step 29.
steps.kashyaTarget: The implication of step 29 that the blood of a dead animal is measured for טומאה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The blood of a נבילה is טהור, as the testimony and the donkey story show, so there should be no reason to measure it.

steps.title: רבי ביבי is silent and is asked why
steps.stepSummary: רבי ביבי does not answer the challenge, and רבי זריקא asks him why he is not responding.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי ביבי was silent. רבי זריקא said to him: Why does the master not answer?
steps.whatsHappening: רבי ביבי has no answer to the challenge from the last step, so he stays quiet. רבי זריקא asks him why he is not answering, which sets up the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The silence means the challenge from רבי יצחק בר ביסנא stands for now and nobody has resolved it. רבי זריקא's question is not a new legal challenge. He is asking about the person: why is a sage like רבי ביבי not defending what he reported?

keyTerms.meaning: He was silent
Answers back, responds
Master, a respectful way to address a sage

steps.confusionAlert: Do not read רבי זריקא's question as a new attack on the הלכה. It is only asking why רבי ביבי is quiet.

phrases.english: He was silent.
phrases.notes: This is רבי ביבי, the one who reported the story about the mule.

phrases.english: Rabbi Zerika said to him:

phrases.aramaic: מַאי טַעְמָא לָא קָא מַהְדַּר מָר?
phrases.english: What is the reason the master does not respond?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי טַעְמָא לָא קָא מַהְדַּר מָר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Reacts to the challenge in step 30. רבי ביבי gives no answer, and רבי זריקא asks why.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why רבי ביבי is not answering רבי יצחק בר ביסנא's challenge.

steps.title: רבי ביבי explains with רבי חנין's teaching on three levels of insecurity
steps.stepSummary: רבי ביבי says he cannot answer, and he quotes רבי חנין's דרשה on a פסוק describing three levels of worry over food. The worst level is someone who depends on the baker for his bread.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: How can I answer him? As רבי חנין said: 'And your life shall hang in doubt before you' is someone who buys grain from year to year. 'And you shall fear night and day' is someone who buys grain from one ערב שבת to the next. 'And you shall have no assurance of your life' is someone who relies on the baker.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי ביבי answers רבי זריקא by quoting a teaching about people who are always worried about where their next meal will come from. He is hinting that this is his own situation, so his mind is not free to answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי חנין splits the פסוק into three parts, and each part is a worse level of poverty. The first level buys a year's grain, the second buys only a week's grain, and the third has no grain at all and depends on the baker every day. By quoting this, רבי ביבי explains his silence: worry over his living does not let him think clearly.

keyTerms.meaning: Grain
Hanging, in doubt
Friday, the day before שבת
Baker, a bread seller

steps.whatToRemember: רבי ביבי's silence is explained by his hard personal situation, not by an answer to the challenge. No reply to the question about the mule's blood is given on this amud.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that a person's state of mind affects how well they can learn and argue in תורה. It also lists three clear levels of living without security over food.

phrases.english: He said to him: How can I respond to him,
as Rabbi Chanin said:
phrases.notes: He is hinting that this teaching describes his own situation.

phrases.english: "And your life shall hang in doubt before you"
this is one who buys grain from one year for the next.
"And you shall fear night and day"

phrases.aramaic: – זֶה הַלּוֹקֵחַ תְּבוּאָה מֵעֶרֶב שַׁבָּת לְעֶרֶב שַׁבָּת,
phrases.english: this is one who buys grain from one Shabbat eve to the next,
